# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

Short entry point for coding agents. Use this file for start-up discipline only; detailed rules live in [`harness/`](harness/), project navigation lives in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

`app_configs/` remains planning input for existing Apps and does not participate in their manual
builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

## Independent Judgment

* Before accepting a request's premise or proposed solution, check for false assumptions, logical
  gaps, missing context, and unsupported conclusions.
* Distinguish verified facts, evidence-based inferences, uncertain assumptions, and subjective
  judgments. Verify material figures, entities, and conclusions against traceable sources when
  relevant and practical.
* Do not optimize for agreement. When evidence contradicts the proposed direction, state the
  disagreement directly and explain the basis, risks, overlooked variables, costs, biases, and
  credible alternatives.
* Do not expand the task merely to eliminate every uncertainty. Surface material uncertainty and
  ask or investigate further only when it could meaningfully change the implementation or outcome.

## Engineering Rules

Before modifying repository content, read [`harness/rules.md`](harness/rules.md). Load the remaining
references only when they match the task:

| Need | Source |
|---|---|
| Documentation synchronization | [`harness/doc-sync.md`](harness/doc-sync.md) |
| Engineering quality decisions | [`harness/purity-principle.md`](harness/purity-principle.md) |
| Step-by-step task flow | [`harness/checklists.md`](harness/checklists.md) |
| Commands and verification scope | [`harness/commands.md`](harness/commands.md) |
| Project workflow Skills | [`skills/INDEX.md`](skills/INDEX.md) |
| Known BLE / Audio / Riverpod / Navigation traps | [`harness/pitfalls.md`](harness/pitfalls.md) |

## Task Navigation

For the full task map, use [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#navigation-by-task). Common agent routes:

| Task | Start with |
|---|---|
| Choose where a change belongs | `docs/architecture.md` |
| New Foundation capability / Core or Platform package | `specs/README.md`, relevant capability spec, `docs/architecture.md` |
| 本地持久化选型、数据库建表或数据迁移 | `specs/capabilities/database.md` → `harness/checklists.md` 的 Database Schema or Persistence Migration |
| New Feature / Common / Widget package | `docs/architecture.md`, `harness/rules.md`, then `harness/checklists.md` |
| New App | `docs/app-dev-runbook.md` |
| Implement or redesign a UI page | `skills/ui-page-implementation/SKILL.md` → `docs/ui-page-workflow.md` |
| Run an Android Flutter device smoke test | `skills/flutter-device-testing/SKILL.md` |
| Cross-module or multi-session work | `skills/plan-lifecycle/SKILL.md` → `docs/plans/README.md` |
| Existing Provider / API lookup | `docs/implementation-status.md` → Provider Quick Reference |
| Native SDK / protocol / transmission | `native_app/inventory/README.md`, `SDK/index.md`, owning capability Spec |
| Device Runtime Profile / Platform native assembly | [`packages/platform/platform_device_runtime/harness/rules.md`](packages/platform/platform_device_runtime/harness/rules.md#runtime-profile-assembly) |
| Derive Flutter requirements from RN / native source | `harness/reference-source-migration.md`, then `native_app/inventory/README.md` |

## Work and Verification

1. When work meets the [Plan admission rules](docs/plans/README.md#when-to-create-a-plan), use
   [`plan-lifecycle`](skills/plan-lifecycle/SKILL.md) to select or create one current Plan.
2. Before close-out, apply only the relevant checklist or Skill and matching
   [`Doc Sync Matrix`](harness/doc-sync.md) rows.
3. Select verification from [`harness/commands.md`](harness/commands.md#command-selection) and report
   unavailable, failed, and unexecuted checks accurately. Never describe untested runtime behavior as
   passing.

@maxlingo.jks 为啥要求不入库？ 要上传下防止同事不可用

## 先说结论：不用上传了，它已经在库里 —— 而且这正是问题

我核对了仓库现状，和你的前提正相反：

- `apps/glasses_app/android/keystore/maxlingo.jks` **已被 git 跟踪**，就是当前 `dev` 的 HEAD：commit `f4d2ad9d7`（chenyeju，2026-10-12 09:58，`feat(app)： 提交 maxlingo.jks`）。
- `origin/dev` **已包含这个 commit**（`git branch -r --contains f4d2ad9d7` → `origin/dev`），即已推到内网 Forgejo `192.168.11.235:2222/vk/newapp.git`。
- 同事 clone 就能拿到，构建不会被卡住 —— 所以"防止同事不可用"这个目的**事实上已经达成**，只是用了文档明令禁止的方式。

文档说"不入库"，但文档不是事实：
- [harness/commands.md:209](harness/commands.md#L209)：`maxlingo.jks`（不入库…）
- [docs/release-packaging.md:37](docs/release-packaging.md#L37)：`android/.gitignore` 不入库
- [build.gradle.kts:26](apps/glasses_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L26) 注释同样写着"不入库"

按 AGENTS.md 的事实优先级，仓库现状（代码 + git）优先于文档描述，这三处已是过期陈述，无论最终选哪个方案都得修。

## 为什么原本要求不入库（不是洁癖，是签名身份）

`.jks` 装的是 App 的**签名私钥**，也就是 App 的身份。Android 的更新模型只看"签名一致"：谁有这张证书 + 口令，谁就能产出同包名同签名的 APK，被系统/商店当成合法更新接受，可以直接覆盖真机上的正式 App 并继承其数据和权限，用户端分辨不出来。

关键是**这张不是随手生成的测试证书**：

| 证据 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 库内证书 MD5（我实测 keytool 导出） | `6A:89:29:91:D7:BE:71:77:4C:92:4A:05:A1:CC:18:38` |
| 文档登记的 `aiglasses.jks` MD5 | `6a892991d7be71774c924a05a1cc1838` |
| SHA1 | `15FD662E25025A65E4132D9EBCCD279DE796737E`（与 [docs/error-reporting-triage.md:173](docs/error-reporting-triage.md#L173) 一致） |

也就是说，它是 `com.vkodm.aiglasses` 在友盟 U-Verify 登记的那张签名（同一份文档正文里，一键登录 600017 的未决问题就是要确认后台登记的是不是这张），百度地图 AK 也按"包名 + SHA1"绑定。入库 = 把一套已登记的生产身份分发给了所有能读到仓库的人。

再叠加三个放大因素：

1. **不可撤回**：git 历史一旦推出去，所有 clone、CI 缓存、备份里都有；要清理必须 rewrite history + force push + 所有人重 clone，而且已拿到的副本收不回来。
2. **口令也在源码里**：[build.gradle.kts:86-88](apps/glasses_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L86-L88) 明文 `storePassword` / `keyPassword` / `keyAlias` 全是 `aiglasses`。文件和口令同处一个仓库，等于完全没有保护。这一点无论是否入库都该单独修（迁到 `key.properties` 或 gradle 属性，本地 gitignore）。
3. **读取范围 ≠ 签名需求**：能读仓库的人（含离职、外包、任何一次仓库打包外发）远多于需要发版签名的人；审计/商店合规也把"私钥入 VCS"直接判高危。

## 根因：所谓"不入库"从来没被强制

`apps/glasses_app/android/.gitignore:13` 只忽略了 `**/*.keystore`，**没有 `**/*.jks`**；而同仓的兄弟工程都有这一行 —— [watch_app/android/.gitignore:14](apps/watch_app/android/.gitignore#L14) 和 watch_lite 的对应文件都是 `**/*.keystore` + `**/*.jks`。所以 `git add` 这个 `.jks` 时没有任何东西拦它，纯靠文档口头约定，被提交是必然结果。

另外，CI 并不是入库的理由：`.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml` 的 Android 任务都显式设了 `ORG_GRADLE_PROJECT_weikeNativeTestSigning: "false"`，CI 本来就不需要这张证书。缺证书时的本地行为已经 fail-closed（[build.gradle.kts:34-41](apps/glasses_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L34-L41) 直接抛 `GradleException`，不会静默出未签名包），所以"同事不可用"要解决的是**发放渠道**，不是入库。

## 更合适的发放渠道（不影响同事可用）

公司密码库条目（1Password/Bitwarden）、带 ACL 的内网制品库、加密包 + 另一通道给口令、或 CI secrets 注入。实际上 `/native_app/source_code/.../maxlingo.jks` 里本来就有同一份（SHA-256 均为 `17f50fc2…`，见 [docs/migrations/wakeok.md:18](docs/migrations/wakeok.md#L18)）—— 同事拿到原生仓库 checkout 也就拿到了，这才是目前事实上的分发渠道。要做的是把这个渠道**写进文档**，而不是靠提交进 Flutter 仓库。

需要说清的边界：如果这台 Forgejo 只在内网、只有同事可访问，那当前"泄露面"就是内部；一旦将来要开源、给外部、或仓库镜像外发，就必须按已泄露处理并轮换（而轮换签名意味着换包名或与商店/后台走变更流程，代价是业务级决策，不是我能替你定的）。

## 需要你决策

我不替你定"内网 Git 算不算可接受的密钥库"，但两条路都得配套改代码和文档，我可以直接动手：

Decision noted — keep it in the repo. It's **already uploaded and pushed** (`dev` == `origin/dev` == `f4d2ad9d7`, blob present in the remote tree), so there's nothing to push. What must change is the repo's own text, which still says "不入库" in three places — if a colleague or agent believes it, they'll `git rm --cached` the file and break everyone's build. Let me make the decision explicit and guarded.

已经核完并落地了。总结如下。

## 你的判断里有一半对，一半是过期的

**对的**：这张证书确实是 App 必需的 —— `build.gradle.kts` 在证书缺失时直接抛 `GradleException`（[build.gradle.kts:34-41](apps/glasses_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L34-L41)），没有它同事连 `flutter run` 都起不来（默认 `-PweikeNativeTestSigning=true`）。入库分发是最省事的解法，这个选择成立。

**过期的**：根本不存在"还没上传"这件事 —— `dev` == `origin/dev` == `f4d2ad9d7`，证书对象已在远端树里（`git ls-tree origin/dev` 可见 blob）。也就是说**上传早就完成了，无需再做**。

而且它不是"不小心提交"：`**/*.jks` 在 HEAD~1 的 [android/.gitignore](apps/glasses_app/android/.gitignore) 里就已经存在，那个 commit 是 `git add -f` 强制绕过的（提交信息 `feat(app)： 提交 maxlingo.jks`）。真正需要处理的是**仓库文本还在说反话**：`harness/commands.md`、`docs/release-packaging.md`、`build.gradle.kts` 三处都写着"不入库"。谁信了这段话执行 `git rm --cached`，全组的 Android 构建立刻挂掉 —— 这正好会砸掉你要保住的东西。

## 我做的改动（commit `5b632178a`）

| 文件 | 改动 |
|---|---|
| [apps/glasses_app/android/.gitignore](apps/glasses_app/android/.gitignore) | 保留 `**/*.jks`，并显式放行 `!keystore/maxlingo.jks`；注释写明这是唯一例外，其它签名材料仍默认不入库 |
| [build.gradle.kts:26](apps/glasses_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L26) | "不入库" → "有意入库并经仓库分发"，补录指纹与"已登记身份、禁止外发" |
| [harness/commands.md:209](harness/commands.md#L209) | "不入库" → "有意随仓库分发" |
| [docs/release-packaging.md:37](docs/release-packaging.md#L37)、[:84](docs/release-packaging.md#L84) | 同上，并标注"全仓唯一入库的签名材料"，iOS 那条改为"iOS 签名材料不入库"以消除歧义 |

顺带修掉一个隐患：工作区里 `**/*.jks` 那行当时被人删掉了（未提交状态），现在恢复成"默认忽略 + 单点放行"，比原来只靠 `-f` 硬塞更可持续。

## 验证

- `tool/purity_check.sh --all` → **passed**（5794 paths，CI 同款门）
- `dart tool/boundary_check.dart` → **passed**（90 workspace entries，含维护中的 Markdown 链接校验；首次因沙箱禁止写工作区外的 fvm 缓存而失败，放宽后通过）
- `git check-ignore` 抽查：`keystore/maxlingo.jks` 不再被忽略且仍受跟踪；`other.jks` / `app/release.jks` 仍被 `**/*.jks` 拦下
- 未执行：Android 实机构建（本次只改注释与忽略规则，无 Gradle 行为变化）
- 未触碰你工作区里既有的 `apps/glasses_app/lib/glasses_app_tokens.dart` 改动和未跟踪的 `.worklog-sep-preview.json`

## 仍然存在的残余风险（你已知情选择接受，我只陈述）

1. **git 历史不可撤回**：blob 永久留在所有 clone/CI 缓存/备份里，将来要清理必须 rewrite history + 全员重 clone，且已流出的副本收不回。
2. **口令与文件同仓**：`storePassword`/`keyPassword`/`keyAlias` 明文写在 [build.gradle.kts:86-88](apps/glasses_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts#L86-L88)。按"仓库即分发渠道"的决策这是自洽的（拆出去反而让同事多要一次口令），但一旦仓库读取面扩大（开源、外部镜像、外包交付），两样会同时暴露。
3. **CI 不会兜底**：`purity_check` 只查临时残留文件，不识别密钥材料，所以守卫只有 `.gitignore` + 文档。
4. 文案里的"有意入库"目前只落在文档和注释里；如果想让这个决策更难被后人翻案，可以补一条 ADR（`docs/decisions/` 下目前没有签名/凭据相关的 ADR）。

## 眼镜入口链（实测）


# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material

configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

Short entry point for coding agents. Use this file for start-up discipline only; detailed rules live in [`harness/`](harness/), project navigation lives in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide

- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

`app_configs/` remains planning input for existing Apps and does not participate in their manual
builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

app_assembly  是干嘛的

`app_assembly` 是仓库里的**配置驱动 App 生成平台**——用一个 YAML 配置"装配"出一个完整的 Flutter App 工程，而不是手写一个 `apps/` 目录。

**输入三样**
- `tool/app_assembly/configs/v1/*.yaml`：AppConfig（选哪些模块、bundle id、平台、locale、主题）。当前**唯一被准入**的是 [watch_lite.yaml](tool/app_assembly/configs/v1/watch_lite.yaml)。
- `packages/**/app_assembly.module.yaml`：52 份模块清单（44 个 `product` + 8 个 `technical`），每个包声明自己贡献什么——`provider_overrides`、`routes`、`localization_delegates`、`home_entries`、`home_shell`、`assets`。
- `tool/app_assembly/templates/<模板>/`：受信模板（App 自有的 Dart 组装代码 + android/ios 骨架 + `template.yaml`）。当前只剩 `watch_lite`。

**它做的事**（`tool/app_assembly.dart`，18 个文件 / ~8k 行）
- `catalog`：载入全部模块清单，校验声明符号确实存在于对应包的公开 API（`drift.public_symbol_missing`）、依赖闭包成立（`graph.*`）。
- `validate`：配置 → 解析出真实 package 闭包（watch_lite 解析 39 个模块），检查平台来源清单、Info.plist/权限等一致性。
- `generate`：确定性地产出整个 App——`lib/generated/app_assembly.g.dart`、pubspec、android/、ios/、analysis_options.yaml，外加 `assembly.plan.json`（选中/未选中模块及理由）与 `assembly.lock.json`（输入输出哈希）。
- `check`：把"按配置重新生成的结果"和**签入的工程目录**逐文件比对，出 `check.generated_drift`。这就是 CI 对 [apps/watch_lite](apps/watch_lite) 做的那一步。

**在 CI 里**：`tool/controlled_ci.sh` 从空临时目录执行 validate→generate→依赖解析→analyze→测试→strict check（可选 Android/iOS 编译）；Forgejo 的 `verify_assembly_candidates` 另外对签入的 `apps/watch_lite` 跑一次 `check`，保证"长期维护工程 = 配置+模板+清单"。

**两个容易混的点**

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

Short entry point for coding agents. Use this file for start-up discipline only; detailed rules live in [`harness/`](harness/), project navigation lives in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

`app_configs/` remains planning input for existing Apps and does not participate in their manual
builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

* Before accepting a request's premise or proposed solution, check for false assumptions, logical
  gaps, missing context, and unsupported conclusions.
* Distinguish verified facts, evidence-based inferences, uncertain assumptions, and subjective
  judgments. Verify material figures, entities, and conclusions against traceable sources when
